item.title: 'It's not just a Cornell problem': Students speak out about sexual assault
item.description: Women are posting videos hashtagged #IAmJaneDoe to support the woman suing Cornell. Students across the country say her case raises concerns about safety on campus.
item.content:encoded: Women are posting videos hashtagged #IAmJaneDoe to support the woman suing Cornell. Students across the country say her case raises concerns about safety on campus.

item.title: For some Brazilians, this election is a vote on Trump
item.description: President Trump says he's been having success winning races in Latin America. As Brazilian voters go to the polls, they're also deciding how much influence Trump should have in their country.
item.content:encoded: President Trump says he's been having success winning races in Latin America. As Brazilian voters go to the polls, they're also deciding how much influence Trump should have in their country.

item.title: France arrests 5,000 people, mostly teens, as school protests spread
item.description: High school students say their classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are missing and buildings need repairs. The protests have spread to cities across France, and some 5,000 people have been arrested.
item.content:encoded: High school students say their classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are missing and buildings need repairs. The protests have spread to cities across France, and some 5,000 people have been arrested.

item.title: Can the Cornell lawsuit force changes that make students safer?
item.description: Universities have responsibilities when students report sexual assault, even if prosecutors don't bring charges. Attorney Baine Kerr explains how those protections work.
item.content:encoded: Universities have responsibilities when students report sexual assault, even if prosecutors don't bring charges. Attorney Baine Kerr explains how those protections work.
item.dc:creator: Henry Larson

item.title: U.S. withdrawal from Iraq is complete
item.description: Twenty-three years after President George W. Bush's campaign of "shock and awe," the U.S. military has completed its withdrawal from Iraq.

item.title: From saunas to psychedelics, how a health reporter sorts science from hype
item.description: A reporting trip to a sauna conference in Oslo found NPR's Will Stone in a sauna with his clothes and recording gear. In this reporter's notebook, he explains how he investigates the science behind wellness claims.

item.title: Medium Build's Nick Carpenter on growing up and finding his way back to fun
item.description: Nick Carpenter, who makes music as Medium Build, talks about his new album "King of Having Fun" and finding moments that make him feel like a kid again.

item.title: Lula or Bolsonaro? Some Brazilian voters say they don't want either
item.description: Brazil's election enters its final day of campaigning as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro make their last pitches to voters. Brazilians explain what worries them, and why some still can't choose.

item.title: The Tonics: suburban a cappella singers are improbable social media stars
item.description: After three decades, an aging male acapella group is building a following by posting video of their rehearsals around suburban, island kitchens. How the Tonics turned social media shade into success.

item.title: How Brazil's two leading presidential candidates are talking about crime
item.description: Crime is at the top of voters' concerns in Brazil ahead of Sunday's national elections. Many are calling for tougher measures — part of a broader rightward shift across Latin America.
